hook: They dropped a 14,000-pound capsule into a pool.
narration: Engineers dropped a fourteen-thousand-pound space capsule straight into a pool.
It was a test version of Orion, the ship built to carry astronauts around the Moon.
Each drop shows how hard the water slams the hull, data that checks the computer models for loads and structures.
The tests ran at NASA Langley in Virginia, before Artemis II, Orion's first flight with a crew.
outcome: The capsule took the hit and floated upright, and the data went into Orion's models.
title: Orion capsule dropped into a pool
description:
In spring 2021, engineers dropped a 14,000-pound test version of NASA's Orion spacecraft into the Hydro Impact Basin at NASA Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, to finalize computer models for loads and structures before Artemis II.
